grouping_guidance: STATUS: COMPLETE (2026-09-01). CONFIRMED sequential-fill structure: slots populate in order (a record with DIAGSEC3 filled will always have DIAGSEC1-2 filled too -- verified directly during the DIAGSEC8/9 investigation, zero gaps found across all inspected records). This means slot number roughly proxies "number of recorded secondary diagnoses" for an admission. IMPORTANT SCOPING NOTE: the official PCDaS ICD-10 chapter/group/category hierarchy enrichment is ONLY built for DIAGSEC1 specifically -- PCDaS's own pipeline does not extend chapter-mapping to DIAGSEC2-9. For case-mix/comorbidity analysis: (a) DIAGSEC1 can reasonably get the same chapter-mapping treatment as DIAG_PRINC if a "primary comorbidity" dimension is wanted; (b) a simple COUNT of populated DIAGSEC1-7 slots per admission is a defensible "recorded diagnostic complexity" indicator -- but per the earlier ChatGPT review, do NOT call this a "comorbidity index" (that implies a validated clinical scale like Charlson/Elixhauser, which this is not). Call it "secondary diagnosis count" or "diagnostic complexity indicator" instead. RESULTS: secondary_diag_count built as planned (populated-field count across DIAGSEC1-7 only). Injury chapter showed an outlier average (1.05 vs. ~0.1-0.23 elsewhere) -- investigated, not just flagged: driven by DIAGSEC1 being systematically populated with Chapter-20 external-cause codes (W19, W99, Y34, V29, etc.) for ~100% of Injury admissions, not by elevated comorbidity burden (96.66% of Injury admissions have exactly 1 secondary diagnosis). This directly cross-validates the Chapter 20 = 0 finding on DIAG_PRINC above -- same codes, confirming the expected external-cause-code usage pattern empirically rather than just by convention.
source: Project validation (12 months, exact missingness confirmed) + ETL-Dataiku-DSS Wiki (official, confirms DIAGSEC1-only hierarchy scope) + project DIAGSEC8/9 investigation (sequential-fill pattern)
